name: Chondrosarcoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Chondrosarcoma

criteria.description: Presence of malignant chondrocytes with atypia and increased cellularity in biopsy specimen
Radiographic evidence of a lytic, destructive bone lesion with chondroid matrix mineralization
Persistent localized pain and/or palpable mass at the affected bone site
Positive staining for S-100 protein supporting cartilaginous origin

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of malignant cartilage cells combined with supportive imaging findings and clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, radiological, and pathological data due to overlap with benign cartilaginous lesions.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized deep bone pain worsening at night
searchTerms: deep bone pain worse at night

pathognomonic.symptomName: Palpable firm mass over affected bone

common.symptomName: Swelling and tenderness at tumor site
Reduced range of motion near affected joint
Nighttime pain relieved partially by NSAIDs
searchTerms: pain at night improved with NSAIDs

occasional.symptomName: Weight loss associated with advanced disease
Fatigue related to chronic disease state
Nerve compression symptoms such as numbness or paresthesia
searchTerms: numbness or tingling from nerve pressure

rare.symptomName: Fever due to tumor necrosis or secondary infection
searchTerms: high temperature due to tumor necrosis

rare.symptomName: Metastatic symptoms such as respiratory distress from lung involvement

searchTerms: elevated calcium due to bone disease

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated alkaline phosphatase
imaging: X-ray showing lytic bone lesion with chondroid matrix calcifications (rings and arcs pattern)
MRI demonstrating lobulated cartilage tumor with cortical destruction
CT scan for detailed bone involvement and surgical planning
other: Histopathology revealing malignant cartilage cells with binucleation and myxoid matrix

distinguishingFeatures: Benign cartilage tumor with absence of cellular atypia
No cortical destruction or soft tissue mass on imaging
Presence of osteoid matrix rather than cartilage
More aggressive periosteal reaction on imaging
Mixed features of osteosarcoma and chondrosarcoma

redFlags: Neurological deficits due to nerve compression
references: Dorfman HD, Czerniak B. Bone cancers. Cancer. 1995;75(1 Suppl):203-210.
Giuffrida AY, Burgueno JE, Koniaris LG, et al. Chondrosarcoma: an update. Orthop Clin North Am. 2010;41(1):29-43.
